title: How work moves through Workcell
description: A goal becomes a reviewed plan, then sealed tests, an implementation, review, and a merge the orchestrator makes on gate output — with blocked work returning to the human and failed gates returning to the builder.

nodes.label: Goal
nodes.sub: a feature · a bug · a refactor · a reported symptom

nodes.label: planner
nodes.sub: investigates read-only · writes the plan and its sidecar

nodes.label: you approve
nodes.sub: the plan, and every blocked or needs-decision return

nodes.label: GitHub milestone and issues
nodes.sub: every issue carries its acceptance tests

nodes.label: test-author
nodes.sub: proves RED is real, then seals the tests

nodes.label: builder
nodes.sub: implements against tests it cannot edit

nodes.label: pull request
nodes.sub: one issue · one workspace · one PR

nodes.label: code-reviewer
nodes.sub: one lens each · no critical or high left standing

nodes.label: integrator
nodes.sub: retests the combined wave, returns the evidence

nodes.label: gate output
nodes.sub: tdd-guard status · gh pr checks · CI conclusions

nodes.label: orchestrator merges
nodes.sub: reads the gate output, never an agent's claim

nodes.label: docs
nodes.sub: READMEs, ADRs, and the changelog match reality

nodes.label: deploy
nodes.sub: a fresh explicit approval · verified · reversible

groups.label: the orchestrator dispatches, holds the human gates, and merges — it writes nothing
